$comment: Shared test vectors for Hallmarq (docs/DECISIONS.md D2). Every package's test suite loads this file so the SDK and the verifier page are checked against the exact same values as @hallmarq/core (F5). Text inputs are JSON strings; every non-ASCII or control character in them is written as a \u escape on purpose (not relying on an editor/formatter to preserve raw invisible characters byte-for-byte). Byte inputs are '0x'-prefixed hex. 'hashing.text[].contentHash' is hashText(input); 'hashing.bytes[].hash' is hashBytes(bytes) with no normalization; 'hashing.bytes[].hashTextResult'/'hashTextThrows' describe hashText(bytes) separately, since bytes go through strict UTF-8 decoding first. The two 'spec' vectors and the 'merkle.abc' example come from docs/Hallmarq_Technical_Documentation.pdf ('Hashing specification' / 'Merkle batch specification'), verified independently per docs/DECISIONS.md D10. Every other vector was produced by running this package's own implementation against the given input, documented case by case in the PR.

text.name: spec vector 1: plain text, unchanged by normalization
spec vector 2: CRLF line endings and trailing spaces normalize away
NBSP (U+00A0) at the end of the text is kept, not stripped as whitespace
a lone CR (not part of CRLF) normalizes to LF
a tab at the end of a line is stripped, same result as the lone-CR case
leading whitespace is kept, not stripped
NFC é (U+00E9, one codepoint) is not normalized to NFD, and hashes differently from it
NFD é (U+0065 U+0301, e + combining acute) is not normalized to NFC, and hashes differently from it
a leading byte-order mark (U+FEFF) in a string is content, not something to strip
empty text normalizes to empty text
whitespace-only text (spaces, a tab, a newline) normalizes to empty text, same hash as the empty-text case
the letter A, used as a Merkle leaf below
the letter B, used as a Merkle leaf below
the letter C, used as a Merkle leaf below

bytes.name: spec vector 2's raw bytes hashed with no normalization, for comparison with the text vector above
invalid UTF-8 (a lone 0xFF byte, never a valid leading byte): hashBytes never looks at UTF-8 validity, hashText throws InvalidUtf8

bytes starting with a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) + "Hello": hashBytes hashes the raw bytes (no normalization); hashText decodes with the BOM kept (ignoreBOM) and gives the same contentHash as the \uFEFF-prefixed string vector above

abc.$comment: The spec's worked example: three items, the strings A, B and C, hashed directly as UTF-8 (their contentHash values are the A/B/C entries in hashing.text above).

single.$comment: A batch of one: root = leafHash(contentHash), no proof needed.

meta.$comment: canonicalJsonStringify's test vector (@hallmarq/sdk): recursively sorted object keys, array order preserved, no whitespace; metaHash = hashBytes(utf8(canonical)).
